newsitem.title: UK: UK to raise net 4.8 bln stg from windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: UK to raise net 4.8 bln stg from windfall tax.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said he would raise a net 4.8 billion stg, including the effects of cutting a levy on gas, through a tax on companies privatised by flotation and subject to economic regulation.
In his budget speech, he said the so-called "windfall" tax would raise some 2.1 billion stg from the electricity sector, around 1.65 billion stg from water companies and 1.45 billion stg from others.

He said the tax would be based on the difference between the value placed on a company at privatisation and "a more realistic market valuation based on its after-tax profits up to the first four full accounting years following privatisation."

Brown, delivering the new Labour government's first budget to parliament, said the tax would be paid in two instalments, the first on December 1, 1997 and the second a year later. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
